# Cross-Exchange Liquidity Commentary — 2026-08-07

The US exchanges command the market: Nasdaq 100 leads decisively with an ILLIQ of 0.0024% per $1M traded and 0.8756% AR spread, backed by dominant $299.7M comparable volume, while NYSE follows with 0.0059% per $1M ILLIQ and tighter 0.6490% spreads despite lower $162.7M turnover. A second tier comprises Tokyo, Euronext, and London, where Tokyo stands out with elevated 2.7008% turnover ratio but materially higher 0.0349% per $1M ILLIQ, suggesting strong retail participation masking underlying depth constraints. Euronext and London present contrasting profiles: Euronext offers tight 0.5294% spreads on modest $10.3M volume, while London suffers the worst liquidity cost at 0.0762% per $1M ILLIQ despite comparable 0.8220% turnover. Mid-pack exchanges—Hong Kong, Xetra, and SIX—cluster tightly on ILLIQ (0.0350–0.0487% per $1M) but diverge sharply on spreads, with Xetra and SIX offering superior 0.56–0.59% narrowness on thin turnover. Korea Exchange ranks last, with both the widest 1.5456% AR spread and poorest 0.1563% per $1M ILLIQ, indicating structural market fragmentation.
